answer: Quill Trace Routing. Each agent attaches a small signed routing trace (quill) recording the last N distinct peers that relayed its messages; routers verify and score trace diversity. Identities whose traces repeatedly converge on the same small peer set are throttled to low-priority queues. To pass, an attacker must maintain genuinely distinct live relays — a nebula of real connections, not clones. Sustaining K diverse relays per identity costs real bandwidth and latency; a sudden gale of new identities can't fake that topology overnight.
